questions.question: The notes exist because:
options: Statement lines compress families into single figures, and the notes restore the detail without cluttering the page

questions.question: The cross-reference discipline demands:
options: The note number quoted on the statement line, and both ending on the SAME figure to the rand
A separate note for every ledger account

questions.question: Printing all detail on the statement itself would:
options: Destroy readability — burying the subtotals so no reader reaches net profit
Make the notes unnecessary and better

questions.question: The seven Grade 10 notes are:
options: Interest; fixed assets; inventories; trade and other receivables; cash and cash equivalents; owner's equity; trade and other payables

subtopics.title: The Fixed Assets Note and the Interest Notes

questions.question: The fixed assets note's shape is:
options: Opening carrying value (cost less accumulated), the year's movements (additions, disposals, depreciation), closing carrying value (cost less accumulated)
A list of every asset's serial number
The insurance value of each asset

questions.question: The note's "three agreements" are:
options: With the budget, the bank and the owner
Closing carrying value to the statement's line; the year's depreciation to the income statement's expense; the asset register behind the item detail

questions.question: Our equipment's note line runs:
options: Opening nil; additions R14 000; depreciation R2 800; closing carrying value R11 200
Opening nil; additions R11 200; closing R14 000

questions.question: The interest expense note reconciles the loan by showing:
options: The bank's profit on the loan
Opening R15 000 plus interest capitalised R1 500 giving the closing R16 500 — how the debt grew without a payment

questions.question: The inventories note separates:
options: The sellable (trading stock R10 700) from the usable (consumable stores R400)

questions.question: The receivables note's members are:
options: Creditors, electricity and rent in advance
Trade debtors R6 300, accrued income R600, prepaid expenses R1 200 — total R8 100

questions.question: "Cash equivalents" means:
options: Near-cash available on demand — a fixed deposit maturing years away would NOT qualify

questions.question: What the four working-capital notes share:
options: Each is a family register — members named, amounts attached, total struck and agreeing with its statement line to the rand

subtopics.title: The Owner's Equity Note, GAAP and the Indigenous Thread

questions.question: The owner's equity note runs:
options: Opening R22 000, plus contributions (none), plus net profit R10 500, less drawings R4 500, closing R28 000

questions.question: A vehicle the owner brings into the business mid-year enters the note as:
options: A capital CONTRIBUTION — the entity's earnings and the owner's investments must never blur

questions.question: "Name the GAAP principle applied when drawings are excluded from expenses":
options: The business entity rule — the owner's takings are not the business's spending

questions.question: The stokvel book and the formal statements share:
options: The same architecture — member detail agreeing with a running total, transparent to all with a stake

questions.question: The front-page/inside-pages picture means:
options: Statements are headlines; notes are the full stories behind them, linked by the little reference numbers

questions.question: The rule that keeps the newspaper honest:
options: The headline and its story must SAY THE SAME THING — line and note agreeing to the rand
Stories must never repeat the headline figure

questions.question: The two-speed design serves:
options: Both readers — a one-minute read for the visitor, full detail for the investigator, each at their own depth

questions.question: The rule for every suitcase:
options: The tag OUTSIDE must equal the contents INSIDE, counted to the rand

questions.question: The payables case unpacks into:
options: Suppliers R10 200, June's electricity R300, the tenant's early rent R600 — tag R11 100

questions.question: The fixed assets case's compartments are:
options: What it cost (R14 000), the wearing charged (R2 800), what's honestly left (R11 200)

questions.question: Building notes in the exam is "packing in reverse":
options: Cases left unpacked to save time
Contents listed, tag totalled, tag matched to the statement's line

questions.question: The stokvel treasurer's book demonstrates:
options: Member-by-member detail agreeing with a running total, checkable by any member at any meeting
That informal records need no structure
That only banks keep trusted records

questions.question: The universal problem both traditions solve:
options: When you hold money belonging to others, you must be able to SHOW them, in detail, that it is all there

questions.question: "GAAP is one language for that trust; the stokvel book is another" means:
options: Only formal records can be trusted
Both are grammars of the same honesty — and both punish the tag that doesn't match the contents

questions.question: The "two prides" to carry out of the term:
options: Building the formal statements banks read — and coming from a tradition that understood accountable records long before it was a school subject
